requirement: The chat window in Arshad.AI blocks the screen — redesign it so it doesn't. Also the overall UI is not mobile-friendly — fix responsiveness across the app.

chat_ui_current_state.summary: Two entirely separate, non-integrated chat implementations coexist. ChatBar is a decorative fixed-footer mock rendered globally on EVERY route; ChatPanel is the real, functional streaming chat but only mounted on the dedicated /chat route.

components.role: Legacy/mock chat input. Not wired to backend — onClick just does console.log(value) (line 26) with a comment '// mock — wired to Anthropic SDK in a future session' (line 25). Has no ChatBarProps fields (empty interface, line 4).
components.rendered_from: frontend/src/components/AppLayout.tsx:19 — unconditionally, inside every protected route (App.tsx wraps ALL routes in <AppLayout>, App.tsx:65-84).

screen_blocking_issues: Line 1-11: .chatbar { position: fixed; bottom: 0; left: var(--sidebar-w); right: 0; z-index: 9; } — pinned across the full viewport width (minus sidebar) at the bottom of literally every page, all the time.
No responsive behaviour: left: var(--sidebar-w) (240px) fixed offset with no mobile fallback.
AppLayout.module.css:7 reserves calc(var(--chatbar-h) + var(--s-8)) (~104px) of bottom padding on .main on EVERY page.

components.role: The actual functional chat surface (SSE streaming via useChatStream.ts, message history, tool-call chips). height: 100% flex column — well-behaved in-flow layout.

components.conflict: When a user visits /chat, AppLayout still renders the mock ChatBar as a fixed footer ON TOP of the real ChatPanel's own composer. Two composer bars stack/overlap at the bottom of the /chat screen — this is the literal root cause of 'blocks the screen' in FEAT-118.

layout_structure.AppLayout: frontend/src/components/AppLayout.tsx renders Sidebar + TopBar + <main> + ChatBar unconditionally, no responsive/collapse logic.
AppLayout.module.css_issues: Line 6: margin-left: var(--sidebar-w) (240px) static, zero media query.
Line 7: padding reserves both --topbar-h and --chatbar-h on every screen size.
layout_structure.Sidebar_issues: width: var(--sidebar-w) fixed 240px, position: fixed, z-index:10 — always visible, no collapse/off-canvas, no hamburger anywhere.
layout_structure.TopBar_issues: position: fixed; left: var(--sidebar-w); right:0 assumes sidebar always full-width; quick-capture input (max-width:720px) has no wrap/stack strategy for narrow viewports.
layout_structure.grids: Dashboard.module.css:36,182,244 and DomainPage.module.css:37,60,93 use hardcoded repeat(N,1fr) with no @media override.
layout_structure.media_query_coverage: Exactly ONE @media rule in the whole app: Obsidian.module.css:94-98 (max-width:900px). No responsive breakpoint anywhere in AppLayout/Sidebar/TopBar/ChatBar.

css_conventions.token_drift: Newer files (ChatPanel.module.css, Login.module.css, ToolCallChip.module.css) use fallback vars like var(--accent, #58a6ff) instead of tokens.css's real names — a pre-existing drift, flagged but out of scope to fully fix.

existing_responsive_patterns.reusable_now: grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(Npx, 1fr)) already used in Integrations.module.css:71, AiEcosystem.module.css:146, HealthFitness.module.css:82 — extend to Dashboard/DomainPage grids.
existing_responsive_patterns.breakpoint_precedent: 900px in Obsidian.module.css — only existing breakpoint value in the app.

naming_idioms.components: PascalCase file = component name, functional only, one per file.
naming_idioms.co_location_with_barrel: pages/AiEcosystem/, pages/Obsidian/, components/FundFlowMap/ use Component.tsx + .module.css + index.ts — follow for any new component.
naming_idioms.hooks: use-prefixed, {data,isLoading,error} shape except useChatStream.ts (streaming/imperative, documented exception).
naming_idioms.chat_dir_precedent: frontend/src/chat/ is an established non-standard top-level dir for chat-domain code — fine to add ChatDrawer/ there or under components/.

recommendations: Eliminate/absorb the legacy ChatBar.tsx global fixed footer. Convert it into a collapsed launcher (small floating action button) that expands into the real ChatPanel on demand, rather than reserving permanent screen real estate on every route.

AppLayout.tsx should not unconditionally render a full-width chat surface on every page. Use a slide-over/drawer pattern: closed = small FAB (~56px, bottom-right), open = bounded-width overlay (~380-420px) hosting ChatPanel/useChatStream.
Deduplicate /chat route: consolidate ChatBar (mock) and ChatPanel (real, SSE-wired) into one implementation using ChatPanel/useChatStream as the source of truth.
Introduce shared breakpoint values (600px mobile, 900px tablet per Obsidian precedent, 1200px desktop) since none exist — decide once, not per-component.
Sidebar needs collapsible/off-canvas mode below tablet breakpoint: hidden by default on narrow viewports, toggled via hamburger in TopBar; AppLayout margin-left becomes conditional.
TopBar quick-capture input needs a responsive fallback (collapse to icon-only trigger below ~600px).
Apply existing repeat(auto-fill, minmax(Npx,1fr)) idiom to Dashboard.module.css and DomainPage.module.css instead of hardcoded repeat(N,1fr).
Reconcile chat UI's ad-hoc fallback color vars with tokens.css's real variable names so the new chat drawer matches the rest of the app.
Any new component (ChatDrawer, MobileNav) follows the co-location pattern: own directory, Component.tsx + .module.css + index.ts, exported <Component>Props.
